title: Autonomous operation of in-space nuclear reactors
bottleneck: A fission reactor on a deep-space mission or planetary surface must operate for years with no human nearby: autonomous startup, load-following, fault detection, and safe shutdown, all while radiation degrades its own sensors and electronics. Terrestrial reactors rely on operators, maintenance crews, and replacement parts; a space reactor gets none of these. Control software must handle scenarios no one can fully anticipate, because a reactor that needs a service call is a reactor that kills its mission.
why_it_blocks: Every nuclear space application — nuclear electric, fission surface power, nuclear thermal — assumes the reactor runs itself; without proven autonomy, mission risk assessments cannot close and regulators will not approve.
current_state: Kilopower's KRUSTY test demonstrated autonomous load-following on the ground in 2018; DRACO will test space operation. Multi-year autonomous reactor operation in space has never been demonstrated.
